Wireframes are inferred from existing Analytics and Settings components; German copy is proposed and insight content is synthetic. ### Reuse and scope Reuse `InsightHero`, `primaryAnalyticsInsights`, `topLeitsaetzeForTimeframe`, `entriesForAnalyticsTimeframe`, and the existing root navigation actor. Keep current thresholds, tabs and time-frame definitions. Offer the opt-in below an available insight once until dismissed or accepted; settings always allows reactivation. Request OS permission only after activation. Denial shows system-settings and permission-recheck actions following the existing reminder flow. Insight notification preference stays separate from timed Leitsatz and Pulse reminders. ### Detection and delivery Persist a baseline at activation so existing insights are not announced retroactively. Compare semantic identity per time frame: Leitsatz belief ID; pattern kind plus emotion/belief IDs. Counts, locale changes, tab changes and pattern cycling are not new insights. Deduplication is lifetime per semantic identity and time frame until deliberate data reset. An insight disappearing and returning does not trigger another alert. Reactivation establishes a fresh baseline. Evaluate only while the app is open, after check-ins and beliefs hydrate successfully, after successful data changes, and on foreground/time-frame rollover. No background computation is required. Imports and restores establish a fresh baseline without notification floods. Activation includes choosing a local hour/minute before enabling notifications. Show 19:00 as an editable suggested time. Delivery always uses the chosen time: persist newly detected candidates and register one non-repeating local OS notification for the next occurrence of the chosen time (tomorrow if today's time has passed). Delivery can occur after the app closes because the notification was registered while it was open. If no new insight was detected, schedule nothing. Do not create daily recurring alerts or imply new insights are generated while closed. Coalesce candidates detected before the pending delivery into one notification, retaining the stable request ID and target. Track baseline, pending/scheduled batch and announced identities separately; successful OS registration means scheduled, not confirmed delivered. Reconcile persisted requests with native pending notifications on next foreground, using an idempotent identifier to recover interrupted persistence/scheduling without duplicates. OS delivery is best effort; do not claim guaranteed receipt. Changing the chosen time reschedules an outstanding batch. Disabling, restore or data reset cancels only insight-owned pending requests. On foreground, cancel invalid candidates and reconcile locale/timezone changes; while closed, the precomputed notification may remain until delivery. Use generic lock-screen text without journal or Leitsatz content. For combined notification taps, choose the stable target by last week, last four weeks, all time; then Leitsatz before pattern; then semantic ID order. Keep IDs in the payload and resolve through the root actor after hydration. If evidence is gone, show normal current Einblicke. User-facing copy: 'Einblicke werden berechnet, wenn du Youmotion öffnest. Bereits erkannte neue Einblicke können wir dir zur gewählten Zeit melden – auch wenn die App geschlossen ist.' ### Implementation Reuse the existing Analytics calculations in a dedicated vertical feature, `src/features/insight-notifications/{domain,application,infrastructure,ui}`. Effect schemas validate notification preferences, semantic identities and the pending batch. Device-local AsyncStorage keeps the notification ledger independent of archive restore and reminder settings; no database migration or new dependency is needed. The coordinator receives clock, storage and native scheduling dependencies through `app-navigation.composition.ts`. Root actor events drive offer, permission, chosen-time and preference actions; the same root resolves cold and warm notification taps after history hydration. The shared notification bridge retains one handler/listener contract. Analytics and Settings reuse existing buttons and confirmed time picker. English/German copy explains foreground computation and scheduled delivery. Native Harness checks actual AsyncStorage and OS queues using the synthetic archive. Consumer and navigation tests cover initialization, failures, retries, lifecycle and tap targets. ### Verification Run `pnpm verify` and `pnpm test:coverage`. Test every insight-kind × time-frame combination; empty/learning states; activation and dismissal; permission undetermined, granted and denied; native API failure; hydration pending, success and failure; persistence failure; imports; duplicates/restarts; changed evidence; ties; week rollover/timezone; disable during delivery; and cold/warm notification opening. Verify consumer behavior before initialization completes. Run persisted-data transactions against the native SurrealDB runtime with React Native Harness, not only mocked query strings. Populate device runs with the committed synthetic archive fixture (133 moments, 15 guiding beliefs), validate iOS and Android interactions, and inspect German layout. Before implementation invoke implementation-delivery and read exact Expo SDK 57 documentation. Cover time selection during activation and scheduled delivery; future time today vs passed time tomorrow; no candidate/no schedule; multiple detections before delivery; persistence/scheduling interruption; duplicate recovery; time change and disable with a pending batch; timezone/DST changes; foreground invalidation; and tap after delayed delivery. On iOS and Android, open with the synthetic fixture, detect a new insight, choose a nearby time, confirm native request registration, close the app and observe the one-shot notification without reopening. Confirm no recurring notification remains and unrelated reminder requests survive cancellation. ---
name: implementation-delivery
description: Use by default for every non-trivial code-changing task, including features, bug fixes, refactors, migrations, UI work, and security changes. Coordinate the work from plan through cherry-pickable pushed commits, verification, screenshots, E2E and adversarial coverage, documentation, handoff, and a review-ready outcome. Skip read-only analysis and trivial edits.
---

# Implementation delivery

Own an authorized implementation through its requested endpoint. Use specialist
skills for their domains; this skill coordinates them and defines completion.

## Plan and route

1. Read repository instructions, inspect the working tree, and identify existing
   conventions before proposing changes.
2. Turn the request into coherent, independently reviewable slices. Separate:
   - dependent work that must run in order;
   - user-only or approval-gated actions;
   - independent, long-running checks that can run concurrently or in the
     background without hiding failures.
3. Discover the skills relevant to the actual work, then load the smallest set
   that materially changes execution. For every non-trivial UI change, consult
   the applicable design-system and platform-design skills before editing.
4. Ask before introducing either:
   - a UI concept without a clear precedent in the codebase; or
   - a new dependency. Show the closest existing code and a concrete proposed
     snippet. For a dependency, explain why existing primitives or a small local
     implementation are insufficient, including maintenance and bundle/runtime
     tradeoffs.

Do not stop merely to announce next steps. Continue through the plan until the
requested outcome is complete or an unexpected blocker requires user input or
new authority.

## Implement in reviewable slices

- Reuse current architecture, UI primitives, and test infrastructure. Keep each
  commit coherent enough to review, revert, and cherry-pick independently;
  avoid checkpoint commits that leave the branch knowingly broken.
- Commit each completed notable slice and, when the user has authorized remote
  publication, push it promptly so the remote branch is a durable handoff.
- Prefer rebasing the feature branch onto its confirmed base and fast-forwarding
  integration when the user requests a linear history. Never rewrite shared
  history or choose an integration method without authority; use the dedicated
  Git integration skill for the operation.
- For dismissible modals, verify backdrop/outside press closes them. Do not add
  outside-press dismissal to destructive confirmations, mandatory decisions, or
  platform patterns where accidental dismissal would lose work.
- When multiple user-visible Codex tasks are explicitly created, prefix the
  coordinating task title with `orchestrator:` when title control is available.

## Verify every slice

- Add permanent automated coverage for each feature at the lowest layer that
  proves its behavior. User-visible flows should also receive E2E coverage when
  the repository can run them reliably; record a justified gap when external
  infrastructure makes that impossible.
- Reuse existing E2E routes to reach changed screens cheaply. Promote useful
  development-time Argent, Maestro, or equivalent flows into deterministic,
  redacted or mocked regression tests when practical. Never store production
  secrets or unredacted personal data in fixtures.
- For security behavior, add adversarial tests that exercise unauthorized,
  malformed, replayed, boundary, and direct-query attempts appropriate to the
  threat model.
- For each UI-changing commit, capture review evidence for every shipped target
  affected by the change. Associate screenshots with the commit SHA in the PR,
  handoff, or artifact store; do not commit diagnostic images unless repository
  policy asks for them.
- Finish with the repository's full relevant unit, integration, E2E, device,
  lint, type, build, and CI checks. A command passing is not enough: confirm the
  documented setup works from its stated prerequisites and that the test
  actually exercised the intended behavior.

Delegate bounded independent checks only when delegation is available and
useful. Give each worker exact setup, ownership, commands, and acceptance
criteria; keep device assignments distinct from other active work. The
coordinator reviews reported failures, fixes code or documentation, and reruns
the affected gate. Do not delegate every command by default or use delegation
to evade approvals.

## Documentation and continuity

- Keep the repository's handoff document current during long work and at every
  pushed milestone. If none exists and continuity risk is real, create the
  repository-standard handoff file. Record branch/base/HEAD SHAs, completed and
  pending slices, exact commands, environment prerequisites, evidence paths,
  blockers, and the next executable action.
- Update user and contributor documentation whenever behavior, setup, commands,
  environment variables, data models, or operational procedures change. Write
  commands so a new contributor or less-capable agent can execute them without
  unstated local knowledge; use placeholders for secrets.
- Simplify the final branch and remove only task-owned temporary artifacts,
  obsolete screenshots, builds, or caches. Never broadly clean shared paths or
  delete another task's files. Ask before deleting `node_modules`. Use Mole only
  for user-authorized machine-wide cleanup, never as a workaround for scoped
  repository cleanup.

## Completion report

Keep the final report compact. Include:

- delivered behavior and pushed commit/branch/PR identifiers;
- data-model, migration, type/interface, public API, and important encapsulation
  changes;
- verification performed and where UI evidence lives;
- documentation and handoff updates;
- skills used;
- remaining rough edges, including conventions stretched and why;
- blockers requiring the user, or explicitly state that there are none.

Do not call work complete while an authorized plan item remains actionable.

name: implementation-delivery
description: Use by default for every non-trivial code-changing task, including features, bug fixes, refactors, migrations, UI work, and security changes. Coordinate the work from plan through cherry-pickable pushed commits, verification, screenshots, E2E and adversarial coverage, documentation, handoff, and a review-ready outcome. Skip read-only analysis and trivial edits.
---

# Implementation delivery

Own an authorized implementation through its requested endpoint. Use specialist
skills for their domains; this skill coordinates them and defines completion.

## Plan and route

1. Read repository instructions, inspect the working tree, and identify existing
   conventions before proposing changes.
2. Turn the request into coherent, independently reviewable slices. Separate:
   - dependent work that must run in order;
   - user-only or approval-gated actions;
   - independent, long-running checks that can run concurrently or in the
     background without hiding failures.
3. Discover the skills relevant to the actual work, then load the smallest set
   that materially changes execution. For every non-trivial UI change, consult
   the applicable design-system and platform-design skills before editing.
4. Ask before introducing either:
   - a UI concept without a clear precedent in the codebase; or
   - a new dependency. Show the closest existing code and a concrete proposed
     snippet. For a dependency, explain why existing primitives or a small local
     implementation are insufficient, including maintenance and bundle/runtime
     tradeoffs.

Do not stop merely to announce next steps. Continue through the plan until the
requested outcome is complete or an unexpected blocker requires user input or
new authority.

## Implement in reviewable slices

- Reuse current architecture, UI primitives, and test infrastructure. Keep each
  commit coherent enough to review, revert, and cherry-pick independently;
  avoid checkpoint commits that leave the branch knowingly broken.
- Commit each completed notable slice and, when the user has authorized remote
  publication, push it promptly so the remote branch is a durable handoff.
- Prefer rebasing the feature branch onto its confirmed base and fast-forwarding
  integration when the user requests a linear history. Never rewrite shared
  history or choose an integration method without authority; use the dedicated
  Git integration skill for the operation.
- For dismissible modals, verify backdrop/outside press closes them. Do not add
  outside-press dismissal to destructive confirmations, mandatory decisions, or
  platform patterns where accidental dismissal would lose work.
- When multiple user-visible Codex tasks are explicitly created, prefix the
  coordinating task title with `orchestrator:` when title control is available.

## Verify every slice

- Add permanent automated coverage for each feature at the lowest layer that
  proves its behavior. User-visible flows should also receive E2E coverage when
  the repository can run them reliably; record a justified gap when external
  infrastructure makes that impossible.
- Reuse existing E2E routes to reach changed screens cheaply. Promote useful
  development-time Argent, Maestro, or equivalent flows into deterministic,
  redacted or mocked regression tests when practical. Never store production
  secrets or unredacted personal data in fixtures.
- For security behavior, add adversarial tests that exercise unauthorized,
  malformed, replayed, boundary, and direct-query attempts appropriate to the
  threat model.
- For each UI-changing commit, capture review evidence for every shipped target
  affected by the change. Associate screenshots with the commit SHA in the PR,
  handoff, or artifact store; do not commit diagnostic images unless repository
  policy asks for them.
- Finish with the repository's full relevant unit, integration, E2E, device,
  lint, type, build, and CI checks. A command passing is not enough: confirm the
  documented setup works from its stated prerequisites and that the test
  actually exercised the intended behavior.

Delegate bounded independent checks only when delegation is available and
useful. Give each worker exact setup, ownership, commands, and acceptance
criteria; keep device assignments distinct from other active work. The
coordinator reviews reported failures, fixes code or documentation, and reruns
the affected gate. Do not delegate every command by default or use delegation
to evade approvals.

## Documentation and continuity

- Keep the repository's handoff document current during long work and at every
  pushed milestone. If none exists and continuity risk is real, create the
  repository-standard handoff file. Record branch/base/HEAD SHAs, completed and
  pending slices, exact commands, environment prerequisites, evidence paths,
  blockers, and the next executable action.
- Update user and contributor documentation whenever behavior, setup, commands,
  environment variables, data models, or operational procedures change. Write
  commands so a new contributor or less-capable agent can execute them without
  unstated local knowledge; use placeholders for secrets.
- Simplify the final branch and remove only task-owned temporary artifacts,
  obsolete screenshots, builds, or caches. Never broadly clean shared paths or
  delete another task's files. Ask before deleting `node_modules`. Use Mole only
  for user-authorized machine-wide cleanup, never as a workaround for scoped
  repository cleanup.

## Completion report

Keep the final report compact. Include:

- delivered behavior and pushed commit/branch/PR identifiers;
- data-model, migration, type/interface, public API, and important encapsulation
  changes;
- verification performed and where UI evidence lives;
- documentation and handoff updates;
- skills used;
- remaining rough edges, including conventions stretched and why;
- blockers requiring the user, or explicitly state that there are none.

Do not call work complete while an authorized plan item remains actionable.
"}

plan.markdown:
---
# Visual plan: open https://plan.agent-native.com/plans/plan-dfdff6a70bc540fc in a browser for the canvas and review UI.
visualUrl: "https://plan.agent-native.com/plans/plan-dfdff6a70bc540fc"
title: "Notifications for new Einblicke"
brief: "Offer notifications for new Leitsatz and pattern insights, with control in Settings."
version: 1
---

### Outcome

Offer notifications alongside an available Einblick and provide a matching settings control. One device-local opt-in covers Leitsatz and pattern insights for last week, last four weeks and all time. Users choose a preferred local notification time during activation. Evaluate insights only while Youmotion is open; schedule already detected new insights with the OS so their notification can arrive while the app is closed. Wireframes are inferred from existing Analytics and Settings components; German copy is proposed and insight content is synthetic.

### Reuse and scope

Reuse `InsightHero`, `primaryAnalyticsInsights`, `topLeitsaetzeForTimeframe`, `entriesForAnalyticsTimeframe`, and the existing root navigation actor. Keep current thresholds, tabs and time-frame definitions. Offer the opt-in below an available insight once until dismissed or accepted; settings always allows reactivation. Request OS permission only after activation. Denial shows system-settings and permission-recheck actions following the existing reminder flow. Insight notification preference stays separate from timed Leitsatz and Pulse reminders.

### Detection and delivery

Persist a baseline at activation so existing insights are not announced retroactively. Compare semantic identity per time frame: Leitsatz belief ID; pattern kind plus emotion/belief IDs. Counts, locale changes, tab changes and pattern cycling are not new insights. Deduplication is lifetime per semantic identity and time frame until deliberate data reset. An insight disappearing and returning does not trigger another alert. Reactivation establishes a fresh baseline.

Evaluate only while the app is open, after check-ins and beliefs hydrate successfully, after successful data changes, and on foreground/time-frame rollover. No background computation is required. Imports and restores establish a fresh baseline without notification floods.

Activation includes choosing a local hour/minute before enabling notifications. Show 19:00 as an editable suggested time. Delivery always uses the chosen time: persist newly detected candidates and register one non-repeating local OS notification for the next occurrence of the chosen time (tomorrow if today's time has passed). Delivery can occur after the app closes because the notification was registered while it was open. If no new insight was detected, schedule nothing. Do not create daily recurring alerts or imply new insights are generated while closed.

Coalesce candidates detected before the pending delivery into one notification, retaining the stable request ID and target. Track baseline, pending/scheduled batch and announced identities separately; successful OS registration means scheduled, not confirmed delivered. Reconcile persisted requests with native pending notifications on next foreground, using an idempotent identifier to recover interrupted persistence/scheduling without duplicates. OS delivery is best effort; do not claim guaranteed receipt.

Changing the chosen time reschedules an outstanding batch. Disabling, restore or data reset cancels only insight-owned pending requests. On foreground, cancel invalid candidates and reconcile locale/timezone changes; while closed, the precomputed notification may remain until delivery. Use generic lock-screen text without journal or Leitsatz content.

For combined notification taps, choose the stable target by last week, last four weeks, all time; then Leitsatz before pattern; then semantic ID order. Keep IDs in the payload and resolve through the root actor after hydration. If evidence is gone, show normal current Einblicke. User-facing copy: 'Einblicke werden berechnet, wenn du Youmotion öffnest. Bereits erkannte neue Einblicke können wir dir zur gewählten Zeit melden – auch wenn die App geschlossen ist.'

### Implementation

Reuse the existing Analytics calculations in a dedicated vertical feature, `src/features/insight-notifications/{domain,application,infrastructure,ui}`. Effect schemas validate notification preferences, semantic identities and the pending batch. Device-local AsyncStorage keeps the notification ledger independent of archive restore and reminder settings; no database migration or new dependency is needed.

The coordinator receives clock, storage and native scheduling dependencies through `app-navigation.composition.ts`. Root actor events drive offer, permission, chosen-time and preference actions; the same root resolves cold and warm notification taps after history hydration. The shared notification bridge retains one handler/listener contract.

Analytics and Settings reuse existing buttons and confirmed time picker. English/German copy explains foreground computation and scheduled delivery. Native Harness checks actual AsyncStorage and OS queues using the synthetic archive. Consumer and navigation tests cover initialization, failures, retries, lifecycle and tap targets.

### Verification and delivery

Implemented on `codex/einblick-notifications`, feature commit `1dd44a9`, pushed to origin. 58 suites / 411 tests pass with unchanged coverage thresholds. TS7, architecture, website and applicable Oxlint checks pass. Full `pnpm verify` stops on pre-existing untracked `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` lint errors; unrelated edits were preserved.

Permanent native Harness passes English/German flows on iOS and Android with the committed synthetic archive and real AsyncStorage/native queues. Actual iOS native picker and background one-shot delivery were verified. Android background delivery remains unconfirmed because its dev-client/bridge diagnostic timed out. No database migration or new dependency was added.

Clean feature checkout runtime verification passes for the confirmed 1.0.4 binaries on both platforms. QA publication to Expo/EAS project `@youmotion/youmotion`, channel `qa`, environment `preview` is prepared but was rejected before execution by automatic approval review, which requires explicit destination authorization. No QA update was created. Older 1.0.3 testing binaries cannot receive these runtimes.

Evidence, exact commands and continuation are in `docs/handoffs/insight-notifications.md` and `docs/qa/insight-notifications.md`. Await upload approval, publish, then verify remote groups/channel and record IDs.

### Decisions confirmed

If overflowVisual is non-empty, some visual comments were not screenshotted because of the image budget; use their anchorDetails and ask for more visual context before making pixel-sensitive changes.
Use recentReviewEvents to understand human edits made alongside comments; event payloads include targeted content patch metadata when available.

# Agent-Native Plans

Agent-Native Plans is structured visual planning mode for coding agents. Build
the plan you would normally write in Markdown, but as a scannable document with
editable blocks mixed in: inline diagrams, code snippets,
open questions, and an optional top visual review area (wireframe canvas, live
prototype, or both in tabs). Architecture and backend plans stay document-only;
UI and product plans start with the top canvas/prototype (the Visual Surface
Choice section owns that rule).

`/visual-plan` is the packaged command and main entry point. Choose the review
mode from the task: UI-first when the work is primarily product UI and review
should start with screens, prototype-first when review should start with a
functional live prototype, design-first when review needs full-fidelity branded
screens, or visual-intake when the user explicitly wants a questionnaire before
planning. When a Codex, Claude Code, Markdown, or pasted plan already exists,
`/visual-plan` uses that source plan as the starting point and builds the review
surface from it instead of starting over.

## When To Use

---
name: asc-crash-triage
description: Triage TestFlight crashes, beta feedback, and performance diagnostics using asc. Use when the user asks about TF crashes, TestFlight crash reports, beta tester feedback, app hangs, disk writes, launch diagnostics, or wants a crash summary for a build or app.
---

# asc crash triage

Use this skill to fetch, analyze, and summarize TestFlight crash reports, beta feedback, and performance diagnostics.

## Workflow

1. Resolve the app ID if not provided (use `asc apps list`).
2. Fetch data with the appropriate command.
3. Parse JSON output and present a human-readable summary.

## TestFlight crash reports

List recent crashes (newest first):

- `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10`
- Filter by build: `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --build "BUILD_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10`
- Filter by device/OS: `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --device-model "iPhone16,2" --os-version "18.0"`
- All crashes: `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --paginate`
- Table view: `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10 --output table`

## TestFlight beta feedback

List recent feedback (newest first):

- `asc testflight feedback list --app "APP_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10`
- With screenshots: `asc testflight feedback list --app "APP_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10 --include-screenshots`
- Filter by build: `asc testflight feedback list --app "APP_ID" --build "BUILD_ID" --sort -createdDate`
- All feedback: `asc testflight feedback list --app "APP_ID" --paginate`

## Performance diagnostics (hangs, disk writes, launches)

Requires a build ID. Resolve via `asc builds info --app "APP_ID" --latest --platform IOS` or `asc builds list --app "APP_ID" --sort -uploadedDate --limit 5`.

- List diagnostic signatures: `asc performance diagnostics list --build "BUILD_ID"`
- Filter by type: `asc performance diagnostics list --build "BUILD_ID" --diagnostic-type "HANGS"`
  - Types: `HANGS`, `DISK_WRITES`, `LAUNCHES`
- View logs for a signature: `asc performance diagnostics view --id "SIGNATURE_ID"`
- Download all metrics: `asc performance download --build "BUILD_ID" --output ./metrics.json`

## Resolving IDs

- App ID from name: `asc apps list --name "AppName"` or `asc apps list --bundle-id "com.example.app"`
- Latest build ID: `asc builds info --app "APP_ID" --latest --platform IOS`
- Recent builds: `asc builds list --app "APP_ID" --sort -uploadedDate --limit 5`
- Set default: `export ASC_APP_ID="APP_ID"`

## Summary format

When presenting results, organize by severity and frequency:

1. **Total count** — how many crashes/feedbacks in the result set.
2. **Top crash signatures** — group by exception type or crash reason, ranked by count.
3. **Affected builds** — which build versions are impacted.
4. **Device & OS breakdown** — most affected device models and OS versions.
5. **Timeline** — when crashes started or spiked.

For performance diagnostics, highlight the highest-weight signatures first.

## Notes

- Default output is JSON; use `--output table` or `--output markdown` for quick human review.
- Use `--paginate` to fetch all pages when doing a full analysis.
- Use `--pretty` with JSON for debugging command output.
- Crash data from App Store Connect may have 24-48h delay.

name: implementation-delivery
description: Use by default for every non-trivial code-changing task, including features, bug fixes, refactors, migrations, UI work, and security changes. Coordinate the work from plan through cherry-pickable pushed commits, verification, screenshots, E2E and adversarial coverage, documentation, handoff, and a review-ready outcome. Skip read-only analysis and trivial edits.
---

# Implementation delivery

Own an authorized implementation through its requested endpoint. Use specialist
skills for their domains; this skill coordinates them and defines completion.

## Plan and route

1. Read repository instructions, inspect the working tree, and identify existing
   conventions before proposing changes.
2. Turn the request into coherent, independently reviewable slices. Separate:
   - dependent work that must run in order;
   - user-only or approval-gated actions;
   - independent, long-running checks that can run concurrently or in the
     background without hiding failures.
3. Discover the skills relevant to the actual work, then load the smallest set
   that materially changes execution. For every non-trivial UI change, consult
   the applicable design-system and platform-design skills before editing.
4. Ask before introducing either:
   - a UI concept without a clear precedent in the codebase; or
   - a new dependency. Show the closest existing code and a concrete proposed
     snippet. For a dependency, explain why existing primitives or a small local
     implementation are insufficient, including maintenance and bundle/runtime
     tradeoffs.

# asc crash triage

Use this skill to fetch, analyze, and summarize TestFlight crash reports, beta feedback, and performance diagnostics.

## Workflow

1. Resolve the app ID if not provided (use `asc apps list`).
2. Fetch data with the appropriate command.
3. Parse JSON output and present a human-readable summary.

## TestFlight crash reports

List recent crashes (newest first):

- `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10`
- Filter by build: `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --build "BUILD_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10`
- Filter by device/OS: `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --device-model "iPhone16,2" --os-version "18.0"`
- All crashes: `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --paginate`
- Table view: `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10 --output table`

## TestFlight beta feedback

List recent feedback (newest first):

- `asc testflight feedback list --app "APP_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10`
- With screenshots: `asc testflight feedback list --app "APP_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10 --include-screenshots`
- Filter by build: `asc testflight feedback list --app "APP_ID" --build "BUILD_ID" --sort -createdDate`
- All feedback: `asc testflight feedback list --app "APP_ID" --paginate`

## Performance diagnostics (hangs, disk writes, launches)

Requires a build ID. Resolve via `asc builds info --app "APP_ID" --latest --platform IOS` or `asc builds list --app "APP_ID" --sort -uploadedDate --limit 5`.

- List diagnostic signatures: `asc performance diagnostics list --build "BUILD_ID"`
- Filter by type: `asc performance diagnostics list --build "BUILD_ID" --diagnostic-type "HANGS"`
  - Types: `HANGS`, `DISK_WRITES`, `LAUNCHES`
- View logs for a signature: `asc performance diagnostics view --id "SIGNATURE_ID"`
- Download all metrics: `asc performance download --build "BUILD_ID" --output ./metrics.json`

## Resolving IDs

- App ID from name: `asc apps list --name "AppName"` or `asc apps list --bundle-id "com.example.app"`
- Latest build ID: `asc builds info --app "APP_ID" --latest --platform IOS`
- Recent builds: `asc builds list --app "APP_ID" --sort -uploadedDate --limit 5`
- Set default: `export ASC_APP_ID="APP_ID"`

When presenting results, organize by severity and frequency:

1. **Total count** — how many crashes/feedbacks in the result set.
2. **Top crash signatures** — group by exception type or crash reason, ranked by count.
3. **Affected builds** — which build versions are impacted.
4. **Device & OS breakdown** — most affected device models and OS versions.
5. **Timeline** — when crashes started or spiked.

For performance diagnostics, highlight the highest-weight signatures first.

- Default output is JSON; use `--output table` or `--output markdown` for quick human review.
- Use `--paginate` to fetch all pages when doing a full analysis.
- Use `--pretty` with JSON for debugging command output.
- Crash data from App Store Connect may have 24-48h delay.

name: asc-crash-triage
description: Triage TestFlight crashes, beta feedback, and performance diagnostics using asc. Use when the user asks about TF crashes, TestFlight crash reports, beta tester feedback, app hangs, disk writes, launch diagnostics, or wants a crash summary for a build or app.

# asc crash triage

Use this skill to fetch, analyze, and summarize TestFlight crash reports, beta feedback, and performance diagnostics.

## Workflow

1. Resolve the app ID if not provided (use `asc apps list`).
2. Fetch data with the appropriate command.
3. Parse JSON output and present a human-readable summary.

## TestFlight crash reports

List recent crashes (newest first):

- `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10`
- Filter by build: `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --build "BUILD_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10`
- Filter by device/OS: `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --device-model "iPhone16,2" --os-version "18.0"`
- All crashes: `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --paginate`
- Table view: `asc testflight crashes list --app "APP_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10 --output table`

## TestFlight beta feedback

List recent feedback (newest first):

- `asc testflight feedback list --app "APP_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10`
- With screenshots: `asc testflight feedback list --app "APP_ID" --sort -createdDate --limit 10 --include-screenshots`
- Filter by build: `asc testflight feedback list --app "APP_ID" --build "BUILD_ID" --sort -createdDate`
- All feedback: `asc testflight feedback list --app "APP_ID" --paginate`

## Performance diagnostics (hangs, disk writes, launches)

Requires a build ID. Resolve via `asc builds info --app "APP_ID" --latest --platform IOS` or `asc builds list --app "APP_ID" --sort -uploadedDate --limit 5`.

- List diagnostic signatures: `asc performance diagnostics list --build "BUILD_ID"`
- Filter by type: `asc performance diagnostics list --build "BUILD_ID" --diagnostic-type "HANGS"`
  - Types: `HANGS`, `DISK_WRITES`, `LAUNCHES`
- View logs for a signature: `asc performance diagnostics view --id "SIGNATURE_ID"`
- Download all metrics: `asc performance download --build "BUILD_ID" --output ./metrics.json`

## Resolving IDs

- App ID from name: `asc apps list --name "AppName"` or `asc apps list --bundle-id "com.example.app"`
- Latest build ID: `asc builds info --app "APP_ID" --latest --platform IOS`
- Recent builds: `asc builds list --app "APP_ID" --sort -uploadedDate --limit 5`
- Set default: `export ASC_APP_ID="APP_ID"`

## Summary format

When presenting results, organize by severity and frequency:

1. **Total count** — how many crashes/feedbacks in the result set.
2. **Top crash signatures** — group by exception type or crash reason, ranked by count.
3. **Affected builds** — which build versions are impacted.
4. **Device & OS breakdown** — most affected device models and OS versions.
5. **Timeline** — when crashes started or spiked.

For performance diagnostics, highlight the highest-weight signatures first.

## Notes

- Default output is JSON; use `--output table` or `--output markdown` for quick human review.
- Use `--paginate` to fetch all pages when doing a full analysis.
- Use `--pretty` with JSON for debugging command output.
- Crash data from App Store Connect may have 24-48h delay.
